opts.t: So you prove the bleed was arterial even though it already stopped
opts.why: If pressure controls it → gauze + pressure dressing to free the hand.

q: Major bleed high in the shoulder or on the neck. What is true in his notes?

opts.t: A tourniquet will not sit above that wound; he named a different option but not the tool
opts.why: Cannot TQ a neck or a high shoulder bleed. Different option — device not named. Not in his notes / don’t invent.

opts.t: A neck tourniquet is the first-line tool he named for core bleeds
opts.why: Cannot TQ a neck or a high shoulder bleed. Different option — device not named.

opts.t: A distal ankle tourniquet will shut off a neck bleed from below
opts.why: Cannot TQ a neck or a high shoulder bleed. Different option — device not named.

opts.t: A tourniquet will not sit above that wound, so leave the bleed for history
opts.why: Cannot TQ a neck or a high shoulder bleed. Different option — device not named.

q: Critical wreck vs a talking chest-pain call at home. Rapid scan?

opts.t: About 60 seconds and shears on the wreck; do not strip the home medical
opts.why: Rapid scan ≈ 60-sec head-to-toe. Trauma naked + shears on critical trauma only. Not a conscious chest-pain medical at home.

opts.t: About 60 seconds and shears on both; strip the home medical too
opts.why: Trauma naked + shears on critical trauma only. Not a home chest-pain medical.

opts.t: About 10 minutes and shears on the wreck; do not strip the home medical
opts.why: About 60 seconds, not 10 minutes. Trauma only.

opts.t: About 60 seconds and shears on the home medical; skip the wreck
opts.why: Opposite of what he said.

q: When did he put the detailed or focused head-to-toe?

opts.t: Later, in the secondary — not during the 60-second life-threat sweep
opts.why: Detailed / focused physical = secondary later. Rapid scan is still hunting life threats.

opts.t: Now, in the 60-second sweep — not later in the secondary
opts.why: Detailed / focused physical = secondary later.

opts.t: Later, in scene size-up — not during the 60-second life-threat sweep
opts.why: Detailed / focused physical = secondary later.

opts.t: Now, in SAMPLE — not later in the secondary
opts.why: Detailed / focused physical = secondary later.

q: You opened the airway and you are breathing for them. Priority word?

opts.t: High only — load and go; there is no low-medium box
opts.why: High or low only. Opened/suctioned airway or ventilating = high. Student “low-medium” was shut down.

opts.t: Low-medium — stay and play; he used three priority boxes
opts.why: High or low only. Airway work / ventilating = high.

opts.t: Low only — stay and play; airway work is not on his high list
opts.why: Airway work / ventilating = high.

opts.t: High only — load and go; but only after a full secondary at the house
opts.why: High = get going; more work en route.

q: Month of belly pain they are just tired of, vs new altered. Which pair?

opts.t: Month of belly is low (still go, no rush); new altered is high
opts.why: Month of abdominal pain = low priority, still transport, not lights-and-sirens. Altered not their normal = high.

opts.t: Month of belly is high (lights now); new altered is low
opts.why: Opposite of what he said.

opts.t: Month of belly is low (still go, no rush); new altered is also low
opts.why: Altered not their normal = high.

opts.t: Month of belly is high (lights now); new altered is also high
opts.why: Month of belly pain is his low example.

q: Golden hour clock he taught for critical trauma?

opts.t: From the injury to surgery; keep it under about one hour
opts.why: Injury → definitive care = surgery, under one hour. Not from 911 or your arrival.

opts.t: From your arrival to surgery; keep it under about one hour
opts.why: Clock starts at the injury, not your arrival.

opts.t: From the injury to your greeting; keep it under about ten hours
opts.why: Injury → surgery, under one hour.

opts.t: From the 911 call to your greeting; keep it under about one hour
opts.why: Not from the call. Injury → surgery.

q: Platinum 10 is which window?

opts.t: You pull up until you start driving — about ten minutes on scene
opts.why: Platinum 10: pull up → start driving away. ABC + board, rest en route.

opts.t: They get hurt until they reach surgery — about ten minutes total
opts.why: That shorter on-scene clock is platinum 10, not the golden hour.

opts.t: You pull up until you start driving — about sixty minutes on scene
opts.why: Ten minutes, not sixty.

opts.t: They get hurt until you greet them — about ten minutes in the yard
opts.why: Pull up → drive away.

q: OPQRST: which pair keeps onset and timing from collapsing?

opts.t: Onset is what you were doing; timing is when it started
opts.why: People blur O and T. Onset = what were you doing. Timing = when did it start.

opts.t: Onset is when it started; timing is what you were doing
opts.why: He split those on purpose the other way.

opts.t: Onset is the 0–10 number; timing is what you were doing
opts.why: 0–10 is severity. Onset = what you were doing.

opts.t: Onset is what you were doing; timing is the 0–10 number
opts.why: Timing is when it started.

q: Pain word. How did he want quality asked?

opts.t: Let them pick a word; do not plant “left arm” or a single leading label
opts.why: No leading questions. Their word. Too many options if they stall. Do not ask if it radiates down the left arm.

opts.t: Plant “left arm” first; then force a single leading label
opts.why: He banned planting left-arm radiation and leading quality words.

opts.t: Let them pick a word; then plant “left arm” before they answer where
opts.why: Do not plant left arm.

opts.t: Skip quality; SAMPLE already covers the pain word
opts.why: Q is OPQRST. SAMPLE is the broader PMH set.

q: Nobody knows the unresponsive park patient. History next?

opts.t: Empty history is allowed; move to the secondary exam
opts.why: No family, jewelry, wallet, or phone data → history is out the window → secondary.

opts.t: Empty history is not allowed; invent SAMPLE before you move
opts.why: He said you can have nothing and still move to secondary.

opts.t: Empty history is allowed; move back to scene size-up only
opts.why: Next is secondary, not a restart of scene.

opts.t: Empty history is not allowed; strip them for a home medical scan
opts.why: Unresponsive park ≠ home chest-pain strip. Go to secondary.

q: They deny drugs. You still think they used. Sunday move?

opts.t: Ask once more with no judgment; second deny → drop it and chart they deny
opts.why: Sunday: may ask a second time (no judgment, not the cops). Deny again → drop it. Chart patient denies.

opts.t: Ask once more with no judgment; second deny → keep pressing until they confess
opts.why: Second deny → drop it, even if you do not believe them.

opts.t: Skip the second ask; EMT meds change if they have alcohol
opts.why: He said EMT meds are not directly impacted. You may ask twice.

opts.t: Call them a liar in the PCR so law enforcement has a quote
opts.why: Chart denies or what they state. LE has their own pathway.

q: You suspect abuse. Report vs defamation, as he said Sunday?

opts.t: Report the suspicion and what you saw; that is not defamation if later false
opts.why: Mandatory report of suspicion. Not defamation if untrue. Walking around naming them an abuser is defamation.

opts.t: Stay quiet; a false suspicion is automatically defamation
opts.why: He said reporting a suspicion is not a defamation problem.

opts.t: Walk the hallway saying they are a child abuser so staff hears
opts.why: That public accusation is the defamation example he banned.

opts.t: Write in the PCR who did it and skip law enforcement
opts.why: Objective observations + quoted statements. Get LE if needed. Don’t accuse.

q: Childbearing-age woman, lower belly pain. Sunday questions?

opts.t: Any chance you are pregnant, and when was your last period
opts.why: Consider all childbearing-age females with lower abdominal pain possibly pregnant. Ask pregnancy chance + LMP.

opts.t: Skip pregnancy; only ask if dispatch said OB
opts.why: He said consider them possibly pregnant on that complaint.

opts.t: Any chance you are pregnant, and skip bowel and bladder on all belly pain
opts.why: Any abdominal pain: also N/V/D and bowel/bladder changes.

opts.t: Ask STD questions on every headache so you do not miss one
opts.why: STDs only if the call fits. Headache is his counter-example.

q: Awake, medical chest pain. Detailed head-to-toe or focused?

opts.t: Focused on the chest; a talking medical can point to the part
opts.why: Focused if you know the part — conscious medical. Detailed if unconscious or significant MOI.

opts.t: Detailed head-to-toe; every medical gets a full strip
opts.why: Talking medical chest pain = focus the chest. Do not need to palpate the whole body.

opts.t: Focused on the chest; also used for the ejected wreck with arm pain
opts.why: Ejected / significant MOI = detailed even if they are awake.

opts.t: Skip the exam; vitals already happened in the primary
opts.why: Full vitals and the physical sit in the secondary. Primary does not replace it.

q: Stepped-on-leg snap, no fall, vs ejected and talking. Which exam pair?

opts.t: Isolated step = focused leg; ejected = full detailed even if they talk
opts.why: Low-MOI isolated complaint can focus. Significant MOI (ejected) = head-to-toe.

opts.t: Isolated step = full detailed; ejected = focused arm only
opts.why: Opposite of the two examples he gave.

opts.t: Both get a 60-second primary rapid scan only and no secondary
opts.why: Rapid scan is primary trauma. This is the secondary focused vs detailed choice.

opts.t: Both skip exam if they can still talk
opts.why: Talking only lets you focus when the MOI is isolated.

q: DCAP-BTLS letters he actually listed?

opts.t: Deformity, contusions, abrasions, punctures, burns, tenderness, lacerations, swelling
opts.why: DCAP-BTLS = those eight injury signs. Joint deformity: assume broken.

opts.t: Deformity, cyanosis, AVPU, pulse, burns, tenderness, lacerations, SAMPLE
opts.why: Those mix primary/history letters. DCAP-BTLS is the injury mnemonic.

opts.t: Deformity, contusions, airway, pupils, blood pressure, GCS, lungs, sugar
opts.why: Vitals are not DCAP-BTLS.

opts.t: Only lacerations and swelling; the rest wait for X-ray
opts.why: He listed all eight and said assume a deformed joint is broken.

q: Which breath-sound split did he teach Sunday?

opts.t: Snore, gurgle, stridor are upper (heard standing); wheeze, crackles, rhonchi are lower (scope)
opts.why: Upper heard in front of you. Lower need a stethoscope on the chest.

opts.t: Snore, gurgle, stridor are lower (scope); wheeze, crackles, rhonchi are upper (heard standing)
opts.why: He put snore/gurgle/stridor up top and the other three down in the chest.

opts.t: All six are upper; EMTs do not auscultate
opts.why: He said EMTs still auscultate. Lower sounds need the scope.

opts.t: Crackles are upper tongue; snore is pulmonary edema
opts.why: Snore = tongue. Crackles = fluid in the lower airway / pulmonary edema.

q: Crackles vs rhonchi, as he paired them?

opts.t: Crackles = fluid / pulmonary edema (straw bubbles); rhonchi = mucus / pneumonia (low rattle)
opts.why: Crackles = edema or drown fluid. Rhonchi = junky mucus, classic pneumonia. EMT does not treat the infection.

opts.t: Crackles = mucus / pneumonia; rhonchi = tongue in the throat
opts.why: Tongue is snoring. Pneumonia was his rhonchi example.

opts.t: Crackles = high-pitched exhalation asthma; rhonchi = upper stridor
opts.why: Asthma wheeze is high-pitched mostly on exhalation. Stridor is upper.

opts.t: Both are upper sounds you hear without a stethoscope
opts.why: Both are lower-airway, stethoscope sounds.

q: First blood pressure Sunday, and a cuff that is too big?

opts.t: First one manual; a cuff that is too big reads falsely low
opts.why: First BP by hand, then machines if they still make sense. Too big → falsely low; too small → falsely high. About two-thirds of the upper arm.

opts.t: First one machine-only; a cuff that is too big reads falsely high
opts.why: He wanted the first pressure manual. Too big is falsely low.

opts.t: First one manual; a cuff that is too big reads falsely high
opts.why: Too big = falsely low. Too small = falsely high.

opts.t: Skip BP under age ten because 90 is only for adults
opts.why: Under ten use (2×age)+70. Under three is usually no cuff small enough, not a hard medical ban.

q: Four-year-old systolic cutoff he calculated?

opts.t: Double the age and add 70 → 78; below that is hypotension
opts.why: Kid line: (2×age)+70 until age 10 (then 90 like adults). Four-year-old = 78.

opts.t: Double the age and add 70 → 90; below that is hypotension
opts.why: 90 is the adult / age-10 number. Four years is 8+70=78.

opts.t: Use adult 90 for every kid; the equation starts at age ten
opts.why: The equation is for under ten. At ten it becomes 90 and you stop.

opts.t: Use 60 to 100; that was his kid blood-pressure range
opts.why: 60–100 was the adult pulse range, not the kid BP cutoff.

q: Eyes open to sound, confused, localizes pain. GCS he walked?

opts.why: Sunday stem: eyes to sound = 3, confused = 4, localizes = 5 → GCS 12. 15 best, 3 worst.
That is a normal 15, not this stem.
Sound is 3 not 2. Confused is 4 not 3. Localize is 5 not 4.
Confused (wrong year) is 4. Inappropriate words (purple) would be 3.

q: Year is 1945 vs year is purple. Which verbal pair?

opts.t: 1945 is confused (4); purple is inappropriate words (3)
opts.why: Confused = a year, just the wrong year. Inappropriate = not an answer to the question (purple).

opts.t: 1945 is inappropriate (3); purple is confused (4)
opts.why: He used 1945 for confused and purple for inappropriate.

opts.t: Both are oriented (5) because they made a sound
opts.why: Oriented is answering the questions right.

opts.t: Both are moans (2) because the year is wrong
opts.why: Moans are incomprehensible sounds, not words.

q: Sternal rub. Localizes vs withdraws?

opts.t: Localize = they know the spot and actively try to stop it; withdraw = passive pull-away
opts.why: Localizes (5): brain knows where; active effort. Withdraws (4): pain somewhere; shrink/turn away.

opts.t: Localize = passive pull-away; withdraw = they know the spot and stop it
opts.why: He flipped those on purpose the other way.

opts.t: Both are decorticate flexion to the core
opts.why: Flexion/decorticate is motor 3. Extension/decerebrate is 2.

opts.t: Both score 6 because any movement is obeys commands
opts.why: Obeys is a thumbs-up / hold the arm out on request.

q: Normal pupil check he wanted documented?

opts.t: Light in one makes both constrict; he charted PERRL / PEARL
opts.why: Conjoined innervation: one light, both constrict. He used PERRL. Book Pearl. Pinpoint classic opiate; dilated many stimulants.

opts.t: Light in one should leave the other dilated; chart anisocoria as always normal
opts.why: Both should constrict. Unequal can be baseline for a few — assume a problem if they cannot tell you.

opts.t: Pinpoint pupils mean cocaine; dilated pupils mean fentanyl
opts.why: Opposite pairing. Opiates → pinpoint. Stimulants → often dilated.

opts.t: Skip pupils; they are only for the medic capnography adapter
opts.why: Pupils are a standard vital. Capnography is the medic CO2 tool.

q: Looks like an OD and they are not breathing well. Test order?

opts.t: Open and breathe for them first; Narcan sits after the field impression
opts.why: Sunday trap: ABC / oxygen before the condition med (Narcan or Epi). Meds are the bottom of the sheet.

opts.t: Give Narcan first; breathing waits for the reversal to work
opts.why: He said people jump at Narcan and miss open/ventilate.

opts.t: Give the EpiPen first; OD and anaphylaxis share one drug
opts.why: Epi is anaphylaxis. Still after ABCs / oxygen.

opts.t: Skip ABCs; field impression always unlocks meds in the primary
opts.why: Impression and meds come after secondary on the skill sheet.

q: Reassess clocks, and a major change in the back?

opts.t: Critical every 5 minutes; stable every 15; major change → restart primary
opts.why: Unstable q5 (almost nonstop). Stable q15. Collapse or ROSC → back to LOC / A / B / C. Pulse back ≠ breathing back.

opts.t: Critical every 15 minutes; stable every 5; major change → start SAMPLE
opts.why: He had 5 for critical and 15 for stable. Major change returns to primary, not history.

opts.t: Critical every 5 minutes; skip vitals the second time; one set is a trend
opts.why: One set is a snapshot. Another full set shows trend.

opts.t: Only reassess after hospital handoff; the ride is nap time
opts.why: He said do not nap. Recheck TQ, splint, pain, BGL, SpO2, restraints until handoff.

q: NREMT medication permission, unless the stem already says you have orders?

opts.t: Treat them as online orders; call medical control before you give the drug
opts.why: Book/NREMT: call for permission first. Real world often offline. Stem “you have orders for aspirin” = do not pick call first. Order: contact → give → reassess.

opts.t: Treat them as offline standing orders; never call on a test
opts.why: He said the test world reinforces the call first.

opts.t: Give the drug, then call, then reassess — pieces in that order
opts.why: Right pieces, wrong order = wrong. Call before you give.

opts.t: Only glucose needs a phone call; Narcan never does
opts.why: He ran all book meds as online unless the stem already grants orders.
